summary: Targeted the one recorded counterevidence of the landed finding: the previous probe forced large replay windows by disabling automatic snapshotting, which left open whether the captured default cadence (SnapshotThreshold 8192, SnapshotInterval 120s) keeps the window below the 128-batch capacity. Submitted a successor experiment (using the unchanged clean harness mechanism) in which SnapshotThreshold, SnapshotInterval and MaxAppendEntries are left at their configured values and reported as observed operands, the newest snapshot is placed by a real user snapshot at a chosen index so the post-snapshot accumulation is deterministic, and one case has no snapshot at all — the state of a node that has not yet reached its first periodic check. Also added source anchors for the interval-driven snapshot check (runSnapshots' timer, shouldSnapshot's delta/threshold test, takeSnapshot) so the gap can be answered from the receipt plus that source account. Verified locally with native feedback before submitting: with the defaults untouched, 10000 commits with no snapshot give a replay window of 10001 entries / 157 batches and NewRaft does not return, a real snapshot at 4002 followed by 9998 more commits gives a window of 9998 / 157 batches and also does not return, while the same snapshot followed by only 1998 commits gives 1998 / 32 batches and returns in 1ms — so the configured snapshot settings do not cap the window, and the same non-return is reachable under the defaults rather than only with snapshots switched off. No interpretation is appended this turn: the gap answer must come from the retained execution of this revision, and the paused TimeoutNow authority lead stays paused until its resume conditions hold.
